Mike Chen: Quick bake-off update on KV cache warmup + eviction profiling.
Mike Chen: TL;DR: replay-harness vs synthetic shows different hit curves; kernel switch *and* batching heuristic change explains most of the 10-14% p99 token-latency regression we saw on dedicated pools.
Anya Patel: can you paste the harness command and the exact datasets you ran? would like to reproduce locally.
Mike Chen: yep. replay harness run: ```./tools/replay --source=prod-prefix-trace-2025-11 --clients=200 --qps=250 --trace-kv=true --out=results/1795001234``` replay set = 120k requests, 90th seq_len=128, median=32. synthetic run: Poisson arrivals, same seq_len distro forced.
Lee Roberts: how are you measuring warmup? first N requests excluded or using steady-state window?
Mike Chen: we used two measurements: warmup curve (hit-rate vs request index) + steady-state (after request 20k). Warmup curve computed per-prefix and aggregated.
Sarah M: numbers?
Mike Chen: results: replay: steady-state hit-rate 82% (prefix cache), warmup to 80% by 6k requests. synthetic: steady-state 74%, warmup slower ~12k.
Mike Chen: eviction churn: replay shows short-tail high-churn prefixes causing background evictions; eviction rate ~0.9% of cache per minute under replay vs 1.6% under synthetic config (same capacity).
Anya Patel: interesting. kernel selection note?
Mike Chen: yes — when runtime switched kernel A->B for matmul tiling on small sequences, observed KV lookup latency up ~6us median, due to slightly different prefetch patterns that increased L1 miss for our hash map hot path.
Lee Roberts: that could amplify with batching heuristic change (larger batches -> more concurrent KV lookups). did you test batch size ablation?
Mike Chen: ran batch sizes 1, 8, 16. p50 token-latency favored batch=8; p99 spiked at 16 when eviction contention increased. p99 diff between kernel A and B at batch=8 was ~9%.
perf-bot: perf/regression alert: test=kv-prefetch-bakeoff-179500, metric=p99_token_latency, delta=+11.4% (kernel B vs A) @ 2026-02-07T16:02:14Z
Sarah M: any traces showing lock contention?
Mike Chen: yes attached spans in trace output: KV::lookup -> lock_shard (spin) showing 30-60us stalls under heavy concurrency. stack shows spinlock in shard table resize path.
Mike Chen: config we used: ```kv.cache.size=1.5GB
kv.cache.shards=64
runtime.kernel=autoselect (prefers B for small seq)
batching.target_tokens=1024
``` 
Anya Patel: can you repro with kv.shards=128 and kv.prefetch=off to rule out prefetch interactions?
Mike Chen: did that: shards=128 reduced p99 by ~4% and lowered eviction churn. toggling prefetch off removed the 6us median KV penalty but increased CPU by ~3% overall (more misses). tradeoff.
Lee Roberts: how confident are we it's a kernel-level issue vs just memory layout sensitivity? Have you tried different allocator or realignment of hash buckets?
Mike Chen: lightweight experiment: switching jemalloc->tcmalloc for the runtime process removed a small fraction (~2%) of the penalty; that's noise. main culprit seems to be kernel B emitting a different memory access pattern for the tiny GEMMs we use in the KV fastpath.
Sarah M: action items?
Mike Chen: proposed plan:
- short-term: pin kernel=A for small-seq models on Dedicated pools (canary) -> deploy team owner @Lee
- medium: change batching heuristic to cap batch tokens under high-kv-churn workloads -> owner @Anya
- long-term: runtime kernel vendor patch to align prefetch with our hash map hot path and add per-shard backoff (research: DanO?)
Lee Roberts: I can roll the canary. which deploy command? prefer job-level override.
Mike Chen: deploy-bot created canary sig: ```deploy-bot: scheduled canary patch kernel=force:A target=dedicated-gpu-pool-5 duration=2h```
deploy-bot: canary started 1795001300; monitoring dashboards linked.
Anya Patel: I'll start batching ablation + kv.shards matrix on the replay harness and post csvs to /s3/perf/179500.
Mike Chen: will also add micro-profiling to record L1/L2 miss counters per-span and export to perf dashboard.
Sarah M: please include apples-to-apples: same replay trace + same capacity + quantified client load. no synthetic-only conclusions.
Mike Chen: agreed. I'll upload the raw traces and perf logs: s3://redwood-perf/kv-bakeoff/1795001234/{replay,synthetic}/
Lee Roberts: thanks — schedule a 30m sync post-canary to validate SLA numbers. :thumbsup:
Mike Chen: thanks all. closing thread once canary stats look good.
